B.LEAGUE Team Box

Source: R/bleague.R
bleague_team_box.Rd

Team rows of the box score of one B.LEAGUE game: the team / coaches row and the team totals, per period category.

Endpoint: GET https://b-league.s3.amazonaws.com/web_json/v2_genius_contexts/{schedule_key}/{latest}.json (the v1 feed, or the game page's embed, when v2 does not hold the game).

Rows with category 2 (team-credited stats; on v1 the row names the head coach in player_id and player_name_*) and 3 (the team totals, whose play_time is five times the period length: 200:00 for the game), one per period_category. The same columns as bleague_player_box(). The v2 totals row carries no TeamID; team_id is filled from the game header.

Usage

bleague_team_box(schedule_key, season = NULL)

Arguments

schedule_key

(integer required): B.LEAGUE ScheduleKey, one global sequence across B1, B2, B3 and every season, e.g. 504734 (B1 2025-26 sec 1, Alvark Tokyo v Utsunomiya Brex); the schedule_key column of bleague_schedule().

season

(integer optional): a guard, the season END year the game must belong to; a context whose Year differs raises hoopR_asset_fetch. NULL (default) = no check (the key alone selects the game).

Value

A hoopR_data tibble with these columns:

col_nametypedescription
schedule_keyintegerB.LEAGUE ScheduleKey (key space: B.LEAGUE games, ONE global integer sequence across B1, B2, B3 and every season). The {schedule_key} every game wrapper takes and the schedule page's list-item id.
seasonintegerSeason END year (2026 = 2025-26), the feed's Year (the START year) plus one.
feedcharacterSource feed of the row: v2 (v2_genius_contexts, B1/B2 from 2020-21) or v1 (v1_contexts: B3, B1/B2 2018-2020, and the 2016-17 / 2017-18 game-page embed). The feeds differ in id types, dates and some codes.
team_sidecharacterSide of the game the row belongs to: home or away.
team_idcharacterB.LEAGUE TeamID as text (key space: B.LEAGUE clubs, stable across seasons AND club renames: 703 = Tochigi Brex in 2016-17 = Utsunomiya Brex in 2025-26). The feed sends a string on v2 and an integer on v1; both are text here. Not a player id.
categoryintegerRow category: 1 = player, 2 = team / coaches row (team-credited stats; on v1 it names the head coach), 3 = team totals. One row per (category, player, period category).
period_categoryintegerPeriod category: 1-4 = quarters 1-4, 15 = first half, 16 = second half, 18 = whole game. Overtime codes are unverified.
team_name_jcharacterTeam name in Japanese (official name, e.g. Alvark Tokyo).
team_name_echaracterTeam name in English, uppercase ('ALVARK TOKYO').
player_idcharacterB.LEAGUE PlayerID as text (key space: B.LEAGUE persons, stable across seasons and clubs: Makoto Hiejima = '8589'). A string on v2, an integer on v1; both are text here. Null where the row names no player.
player_nocharacterShirt number as text, so '00' and '0' stay distinct; null on team and game-level rows.
player_name_jcharacterPlayer name in Japanese (katakana for foreign players); null on team and game-level rows.
player_name_echaracterPlayer name in English ('Makoto Hiejima'); null on team and totals rows.
play_timecharacterMinutes played as the feed's 'mm:ss'; 'DNP' = did not play. Totals rows hold 5 x the period length ('200:00' for the game).
on_courtlogicalTrue for the five players on court when the context was last written (for a final game, at the final buzzer); the same value on every period row of the player. Null on v2 team and totals rows.
display_orderintegerDisplay order of the row (v1 only), integer; null on v2.
starterlogicalTrue when the player started; false for the bench; null on team and totals rows. (The feed sends 1 / null on v2 and a boolean on v1.)
seconds_playedintegerTime on court in seconds, parsed from play_time (50:00 = 3000); null for DNP and blank.
pointsintegerPoints scored. The v2 feed sends ” (a placeholder, not 0) on the team row of quarters; null here.
fg3_madeintegerThree-point field goals made (v2 placeholder ” on quarter team rows becomes null).
fg3_attemptedintegerThree-point field goals attempted.
fg2_madeintegerTwo-point field goals made.
fg2_attemptedintegerTwo-point field goals attempted.
ft_madeintegerFree throws made.
ft_attemptedintegerFree throws attempted.
foulsintegerPersonal fouls committed (F).
fouls_drawnintegerFouls drawn (FD).
reb_offintegerOffensive rebounds (OR).
reb_defintegerDefensive rebounds (DR).
rebintegerTotal rebounds.
turnoversintegerTurnovers (TO).
assistsintegerAssists credited to the player or team (AS).
stealsintegerSteals credited to the player or team (ST).
blocksintegerBlocks made (BS).
blocks_receivedintegerShots of this player or team that were blocked (BSON).
ptfbintegerFast-break figure; equals the summary's fast-break points on the one game checked, but whether it counts points or baskets is unverified.
pt2inintegerInside-the-paint figure: on v2 a COUNT of made inside-the-paint 2PT (the summary holds 2x that in points); on v1 points in the paint (0 on B3, whose 2PT shots are never split by paint).
pt2ndintegerSecond-chance figure; smaller than the summary's second-chance points, so likely made baskets; unverified.
ptpftintegerPoints off turnovers; v1 box rows only, null on v2.
dunksintegerDunks made (PT2DUNK); v1 box rows only, null on v2.
efficiencyintegerEfficiency rating (kokendo), era-dependent: v2 = points + rebounds + assists + steals + blocks + fouls drawn - missed FG - missed FT - turnovers - fouls - shots blocked (PIR); v1 omits fouls drawn, fouls and shots blocked.
plus_minusintegerPlus/minus: team point difference while on court. v2 from 2022-23 only; null on totals and half rows.
ast_todoubleAssist-to-turnover ratio (0 when no turnovers). v2 from 2022-23 only; null on half rows.
efgdoubleEffective field-goal percentage as a FRACTION 0-1 (3PT weighted 1.5x); the site multiplies by 100. v2 from 2022-23 only.
tsdoubleTrue-shooting percentage as a FRACTION 0-1; the site multiplies by 100. v2 from 2022-23 only.
usgdoubleUsage rate in PERCENT 0-100. v2 from 2022-23 only; absent on totals rows.
off_rtgdoubleOffensive rating. v2 from 2022-23 only; on team and totals rows 0 in every sample, never filled.
def_rtgdoubleDefensive rating. v2 from 2022-23 only; on team and totals rows 0 in every sample, never filled.
net_rtgdoubleNet rating. v2 from 2022-23 only; on team and totals rows 0 in every sample, never filled.
possdoublePossessions. v2 from 2022-23 only; on team and totals rows 0 in every sample, never filled.

Details

The B.LEAGUE (Japan Professional Basketball League: B1, B2, B3) wrappers mirror sdv-py's sportsdataverse.basketball.bleague wrappers of the same names: same arguments, the same snake_case columns and types, one row per sdv-py row.

Unofficial and unsupported. The game contexts are JSON objects in B.LEAGUE's own public S3 bucket (b-league.s3.amazonaws.com, the store its game pages read), and the schedule, standings and game_detail pages of www.bleague.jp are parsed here. Neither host publishes terms for this use (the site's /terms/ answers 404; robots.txt sets a Crawl-delay only for msnbot and bingbot). Requests are spaced at least one second apart per host; 429 and 5xx answers are retried (three attempts). SportsDataverse has not ruled on the site's terms, so the data is not redistributed as release assets.

Seasons are END years (season = 2026 is 2025-26); the site's own Year / year= is the START year, so the request sends year = season - 1. Game wrappers take the global schedule_key (one integer sequence across B1, B2, B3 and every season: 1 = the 2016-17 opener, 5856 in 2020-21, 500017 in 2022-23, 504734 / 505508 B1 / B2 and 10693 B3 in 2025-26); list a day's keys with bleague_schedule().

Feeds. A game is read from the v2 feed (B1/B2 from 2020-21), else the v1 feed (B3 and B1/B2 2018-2020), else the game page's embedded copy (the only source of 2016-17 and 2017-18), decided at run time. v2 ids are strings, v1 ids integers: both become text here. v1 adds leaders and the score track; the team-rebound codes 18 / 19 are swapped between the feeds and a v1 substitution is one row where v2 has two. Player and team names are Japanese (English names only on the box score and header). Game wrappers serve FINISHED games only. Each game wrapper fetches the context itself (two requests): fetch once per game per wrapper you need.

Errors are classed conditions, never a warning plus an empty frame: hoopR_no_data (no source holds the game, a schedule day without games, HTTP 404), hoopR_bad_request (a non-integer or out-of-range argument, HTTP 400 / 422) and hoopR_asset_fetch (any other failure: another status, a transport error, a non-JSON or non-HTML body, an error or changed body, an unfinished game, a context or page for another game, season, tab or day, a truncated schedule list, or layout drift). All inherit hoopR_error.
